newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gene maize seed supplier bemoans French delay.
newsitem.headline: Gene maize seed supplier bemoans French delay.

text.p: French delays to the approval of gene-altered maize cultivation in Europe are a setback for potential seed suppliers, a spokeswoman for Novartis Agro GmbH in Frankfurt said.
"We have to assume the process will be delayed by another year," she said.
French farm minister Philippe Vasseur said earlier today the cultivation of maize would not be allowed this year .

Although France recently cleared the marketing of imported transgenic maize in the EU, it stopped short of allowing plantings here amid concern too little is known about possible health and environmental risks.
The French decision mostly hits Novartis subsidiaries, which were planning commercial sales for 1997 plantings.
Novartis in Germany, a smaller market for maize, had already decided to restrict itself to trial runs this year, the spokeswoman said.
It would continue to test two gene maize varieties, Pactol and Cesar, with view to German sowings next year.
Swiss-based Novartis group emerged last year as a result of a Ciba Geigy and Sandoz AG SANZ.S merger.
Developed by Swiss firm Ciba-Geigy and adapted to resist the corn borer pest, the controversial new maize is grown in the U.S. and imports have arrived in the EU.
As parts of the EU public are hostile to genetically engineered crops, Luxembourg and Austria have unilaterally banned both sales and cultivation of gene maize.
Bonn farm ministry officials said they did not expect Germany to become the driving force in resolving the problem which was now largely dominated by labelling issues.
"The EU Commission will have to mediate an end to the discussions, " one said.
